messages:
vivian: Heads up — DSAR received for user user+privacy@acme. Legal attached attestation. They want full erasure (embeddings + PII). Filing here to coordinate RBAC/audit/KMS pieces before we act. Can folks owning the delete pipeline weigh in?

anita: Noted. There's currently a retention exception for billing logs for acme-tenant until 2026-07-01 — legal needs to confirm we can override for a SAR. Also need to confirm backups/snapshots scope.

kevin: Quick overview of our current flow: live API marks records soft-deleted (deleted_at) -> background scrubbing job hard-deletes content + removes vector index entries -> snapshots have their own TTL (90d) and a separate purge job. For a DSAR we need manual hard-delete + snapshot purge. KMS: keys are customer-managed; deletion of ciphertext doesn't remove key material. If keys are scheduled for rotation, ensure we don't rely on key destruction for erasure.

sam: Typical runbook I propose:
1) Check legal hold flag (if on hold, STOP).
2) Freeze retention exception for tenant (if any).
3) Create ephemeral forensic export if legal requests (store in restricted bucket).
4) Run privacy-sweep job with --force-delete --purge-snapshots for tenant.
5) Verify audit logs emitted to SIEM (PRIV_DELETE event) and KMS key usage entries.
6) Close ticket and publish confirmation to requester.

kevin: Example command I'll run after legal clears: ```./bin/privacy-sweep --tenant acme --datasets embeddings,profile_pii --purge-snapshots --emit-audit PRIV_DELETE```

kevin: Notes on audit: we must ensure storage.delete, kv-index.delete, and kms:cryptoDelete or kms:usage events are ingested. SIEM mapping currently expects event_type=PRIV_DELETE and field deleted_by_service_account. If any of those are missing, we need SIEM parsing update.

legal-bot: Legal: SAR attestation checked. No legal hold on this user. Approver: @jordan-legal signed off at 2026-04-02T14:12Z. Proceed with erasure.

vivian: Great — legal gives go. @kevin can you run after 14:00 UTC and post status here? Also open a retention-exception-cancel ticket (so we don't auto-restore).

kevin: Will run at 14:10 UTC. Kicking off now. Posting job id: psweep-2790011223-01. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

deploy-bot: Job queued: psweep-2790011223-01 by kevin. ETA ~8m.

kevin: psweep job finished. Summary: 1. 12k embedding vectors hard-deleted; 2. 3 snapshot manifests removed (backup-bucket eu-west-1); 3. Audit events emitted -> PRIV_DELETE x12k, kms:Encrypt/Decrypt entries present. Logs -> https://logs.internal/psweep/2790011223 

sam: I'll run quick verification queries after job finish: ```SELECT count(*) FROM embeddings WHERE tenant='acme' AND deleted_at IS NULL;``` expecting 0. Also validate snapshot manifests absent in backup-bucket.

sam: Verification done. Queries return 0 live embeddings for tenant acme. Snapshot manifests removed. SIEM shows PRIV_DELETE with matching task_id psweep-2790011223-01. All good. :thumbsup:

vivian: Thanks team — I'll update DSAR tracker and notify requester. Filing a short postmortem in case retention-exception workflow needs tuning.

anita: One follow-up: we should add an RBAC check to ensure only the privacy-service principal can run --purge-snapshots. Ticket: ENGSEC-priv-289.

kevin: Agreed. I'll add IAM policy lock and a monitoring alert if non-privacy principals call PRIV_DELETE.

vivian: Closing out here. Excellent coordination.
